Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
13 photos
Photo: Honda
It's been almost two years to the date since Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) announced during the 2024 SEMA show it is officially entering the performance parts business, and we were kind of losing hope of seeing that anytime soon. Luckily, this year's SEMA is fast approaching, and with it so do the first HRC parts designed in-house.
The company decided to start its adventure into this segment with new sets of forged wheels and a tuned exhaust system. These parts are meant to be used on a number of higher-spec Honda and Acura models, including the Civic Type R, Integra Type S, and Passport TrailSport.
There will be two new wheel sets available for the cars mentioned above. The first set, intended for the 2023 and newer Honda Civic Type R and the 2024 and newer Acura Integra Type S, comes in at 19 inches and is made of aluminum.
The wheels have been designed by Honda with help from Italian company 2elle-engineering, which supplies the wheels for the ARX-06 race car. Fitted with thin spokes, the wheels can be had in either gray or bronze.
What makes these wheels special is the fact that they weigh almost 21 pounds (9.5 kg), and that can have a serious impact on the way the Hondas they are meant for handle and perform while on the track.
The second wheel set is a tad smaller, coming in at 18 inches. Made of forged aluminum, these bits of hardware are meant to be used in off-road settings, meaning they have been specifically designed for the 2026 Honda Passport and the 2023 and newer Honda Pilot .
They were made with assistance from Titan 7, which supplies the wheels for Honda Racing's Pikes Peak International Hill Climb and other production-based race car efforts. Compared to the factory wheels fitted on the two SUVs, they can handle 220 pounds (100 kg) more load.
Last but not least, HRC is introducing next month at SEMA a new, tuned cat-back exhaust developed together with Borla. The stainless-steel piece of hardware is designed for the same Passport and Pilot models, and it is supposed to increase both their performance and sound.
The exhaust comes with six percent more flow rate and is fitted with Borla's so-called polyphonic harmonizer that boosts the sound of the double-overhead cam 3.5-liter V6 it can be tied to. As a twist, it is also smaller than the factory one, and that translates into a ground clearance increase of some 1.9 inches (five cm).
Honda Racing will bring these new parts to the SEMA show at the beginning of November, where it will also preview the next parts that will enter the catalogue later on: among them, adjustable coilovers with camber plates, a big Brembo brake kit with 6-piston callipers, and a short-throw shifter.
